title: Translate OpenAI ChatCompletions -> Redwood API (streaming + function calls)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a translation/proxy layer that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions v1 requests and converts them to Redwood's internal /generate/chat API and back. Goals: preserve streaming semantics (token deltas), support function/tool calling semantics including partially streamed arguments, map errors and rate-limit headers cleanly, and ensure minimal latency and minimal payload transformation for high-throughput use cases. This work is intended to help customers migrate quickly from OpenAI-compatible clients while taking advantage of Redwood routing, model fallbacks, and cost controls.
background_and_rationale: Many enterprise customers have existing code that calls the OpenAI Chat Completions API and expect the same streaming events, function call behavior, and response shapes. Our hosted API offers superior cost/latency, but mismatch in streaming shapes (delta events, function-call chunking) caused earlier regressions. Prior tickets (ENG-5400, ENG-8127, ENG-9371) built the initial compatibility shims; this ticket revisits the proxy for robust handling of edge cases: partial JSON function arguments across delta frames, assistant role name normalization, assistant->tool role mapping, and structured output enforcement when a schema is provided.
implementation_notes: Architecture: a stateless translation layer placed in front of the generation service. For streaming: translate OpenAI 'delta' chunks to our SSE/chunked JSON streaming format while preserving token order and stable 'id' mapping. For function/tool calls: collect 'function_call' deltas until closed and emit a consolidated tool_call event to the runtime, but also emit intermediate partial events to clients that expect them. Reassembly strategy: buffer function 'arguments' fragments per-request using a size-limited accumulator and JSON-safe concatenation; if we detect malformed JSON after a size limit, fall back to passing raw concatenated string in a 'tool_partial' meta field and surface a user-visible warning. Error mapping: 429 -> 429 with X-RateLimit-* headers translated; model not-found -> 404 with helpful message and suggested model aliases. Backwards compatibility: keep original OpenAI top-level fields (id, object, created) in responses and include Redwood metadata under 'redwood_meta' in response but only when the client sends X-Redwood-Debug header.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions request payloads (messages, temperature, max_tokens, functions schema, function_call) and returns semantically equivalent responses for non-streaming mode
Streaming clients receive delta events with the same sequence semantics as OpenAI (content, role, function_call chunks). We must pass the OpenAI streaming test harness without reordering tokens

Function/tool calls that stream arguments across multiple deltas are reassembled to a valid JSON payload and delivered to the runtime; if reassembly fails, a deterministic fallback is used and client receives a warning field
Automated tests cover: partial-argument streaming, malformed argument recovery, role mapping (assistant/system/user), error header translation, and rate-limit behavior
Latency regression <5% p95 when proxy enabled vs direct Redwood API for representative workloads
Documentation updated with migration notes and contract differences (including headers and redwood_meta visibility)
test_plan: Unit tests for translator: token/delta -> chunk conversion, function argument accumulation, header mapping
Integration tests using the OpenAI streaming test harness and a mock Redwood runtime to validate event order and partial function streams
Load test with synthetic chat workloads (burst and sustained) to validate p95 latency and memory bounds on per-request buffers
Chaos test: simulate truncated streams and ensure deterministic fallback behavior and no server-side leaks
